# SUP menu build: separability report

## Scope and evidence

This is static source analysis, not a successful build, browser regression test or verification of the live deployment. `src/BUILD.md` is the pipeline authority; it explicitly separates building from publication. (`src/BUILD.md:3–11`)

Citation paths use these roots:

- **Repository:** `/Users/jameshan/Projects/sup-noodle-bar-menu`
- **D/**: `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-jameshan/178a112a-834c-45cb-ab99-3b334043d363/scratchpad/kei/`
- **N**: `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-jameshan/178a112a-834c-45cb-ab99-3b334043d363/scratchpad/phase2-notes.md`

**Concurrent-change limitation:** `src/template.html` changed during inspection. Its citations below reference the version read at **2026-09-14 22:48:29 UTC**, SHA-256 `d26908d62ede833247cf806c5929be95da3050db8d165a49a5f4f13493b87590`. These are audit observations; later edits may move line numbers.

## Executive findings

1. **Yes: the print renderer can produce PDFs without executing the web build, worker generation or QR step.** Its executable entry point calls its own HTML renderer and Chrome PDF exporter. However, its revision calculation still reads web/worker/QR **source files**. Execution is separable today; a minimal print-only source distribution requires changes to the shared input manifest. (`src/build_print.py:2–8`, `src/build_print.py:189–195`, `src/build_common.py:10–12`, `src/build_common.py:26–41`)

2. **All seven other-brand drafts exist on disk.** They are English review workspaces with generated HTML and PDF artifacts. They are not thirteen-language equivalents of SUP. (`D/vox/README.md:1–12`, `D/nep/PRD.md:15–19`, `D/kin/PRD.md:3`, `D/rol/REPORT.md:3–9`, `D/ini/REPORT.md:3–15`, `D/kei-coffee/data/SCHEMA-NOTES.md:3`, `D/qua/REPORT.md:3–13`)

3. **The current release command has no tier switch.** It always executes web rendering, print rendering and site packaging; packaging always generates the QR/card and worker. Smaller products require orchestration and gate changes, not a different command-line option already present. (`src/release.py:135–149`, `src/build_site.py:27–46`)

4. **The largest shared migration problem is content semantics.** The drafts introduce unknown prices, location/daypart distinctions, richer modifiers and different allergen-certainty rules. SUP’s renderers do not implement those contracts. (`D/nep/data/SCHEMA-NOTES.md:18–29`, `D/vox/data/SCHEMA-NOTES.md:45–57`, `D/rol/data/SCHEMA-NOTES.md:16–23`, `src/build_print.py:15–19`, `src/template.html:434`, `src/template.html:469–470`)

5. **Seven sibling paths do not inherently break SUP’s worker guard.** Copying SUP’s cache names, root paths or release-tree assumptions into those siblings can break isolation and SUP’s offline behavior. (`src/sup-worker.js:3–17`, `src/sup-worker.js:48–50`, `src/sup_sw.py:5–9`, `src/build_site.py:10–17`)

### Checkout discrepancies affecting this inventory

- The executable release script is under `src/`; its `ROOT` resolves to that directory. The documented command is therefore relative to that build workspace, and its output replacement targets are there. (`src/release.py:18`, `src/release.py:153–162`, `src/BUILD.md:3`)
- At inspection, `src/render` was absent. `verify_pdfs.py` nevertheless requires that exact executable. Its functioning in this checkout is **unverified**; release instead uses Poppler directly. (`src/verify_pdfs.py:17`, `src/release.py:115–125`)
- At inspection, `src/research/toast-out.json` was absent; the saved SUP extraction was under `docs/toast-out.json`. The importer uses a current-working-directory-relative `research/toast-out.json`. (`src/merge_toast.py:2`, `docs/toast-out.json:2–10`)
- At inspection, the repository lacked the test reports linked by `src/BUILD.md`, and no project PRD was found there. Existing draft workspaces do contain PRDs. Consequently, the cited regression history was **not verified from this checkout**. (`src/BUILD.md:36–40`, `D/vox/PRD.md:1–3`, `D/nep/PRD.md:1–3`)

## 3. Hard-coded SUP assumptions

### 3.1 Identity, content and rendering contracts

| Assumption | Locations and consequence |
|---|---|
| SUP name and location tagline | English title, brand and tagline are explicit; static web title, image alternative text and masthead also say SUP. Print document title and footer have additional literal names. (`src/strings.en.json:2–4`, `src/template.html:8–16`, `src/template.html:377`, `src/build_print.py:105`, `src/build_print.py:115`, `src/qrcard.html:2`) |
| SUP identity in all thirteen catalogs | Each locale begins with SUP title/brand/tagline, and each contains SUP-specific promotion terms. These need content replacement, not merely a changed logo. (`src/strings.en.json:2–4`, `src/strings.es.json:2–4`, `src/strings.vi.json:2–4`, `src/strings.ko.json:2–4`, `src/strings.zh.json:2–4`, `src/strings.zh-Hant.json:2–4`, `src/strings.tl.json:2–4`, `src/strings.fa.json:2–4`, `src/strings.ar.json:2–4`, `src/strings.ja.json:2–4`, `src/strings.ru.json:2–4`, `src/strings.hi.json:2–4`, `src/strings.ur.json:2–4`) |
| One shared menu despite two displayed restaurants | Renderers iterate all sections without location resolution; both contacts are then displayed. This does not implement location-specific prices or catalogs. (`src/build_print.py:101–105`, `src/template.html:577–578`, `src/template.html:641–642`) |
| SUP sections and dish identifiers | Structure contains `appetizers`, `pho`, `plates`, `extras`, `kids`, `drinks`; renderers consume those IDs. The observed 43 items are data, not a renderer limit. (`src/structure.json:15`, `src/structure.json:176`, `src/structure.json:403`, `src/structure.json:643`, `src/structure.json:719`, `src/structure.json:740`, `src/build_print.py:76–84`) |
| Fixed promotion model | `lunch` means the lunch-specific UI keys; **every other special** is rendered using kimchi keys. Structure fixes the featured item to `phobeefbelly`, regular price 16 and offer 11.99, plus a kimchi card. (`src/structure.json:890–900`, `src/build_print.py:85–93`, `src/template.html:548–557`, `src/sup_nojs.py:26–31`) |
| SUP promotion and refill copy | Weekday lunch terms, SUP-wide applicability, pho refills and kimchi options are stored in the dictionaries. A section named `drinks` automatically receives the refill note. (`src/strings.en.json:26–37`, `src/strings.en.json:48`, `src/strings.en.json:60–61`, `src/build_print.py:81`, `src/template.html:568`, `src/sup_nojs.py:36`) |
| Section presentation tied to IDs | `extras`, `kids` and `drinks` receive compact web layout; `lunch` receives special badge styling. (`src/template.html:503`, `src/template.html:564`) |
| SUP allergy/raw-food/halal policy copy | These are content assertions, not generic engine defaults. Halal text is rendered only for Arabic, Persian and Urdu. (`src/strings.en.json:43–47`, `src/build_print.py:107–109`, `src/template.html:580–582`) |
| Nine-category allergen vocabulary | SUP fixes the initial category order; the importer maps wheat to `gluten`. Drafts introduce additional or differently interpreted categories. (`src/structure.json:2–11`, `src/merge_toast.py:3`, `D/vox/data/SCHEMA-NOTES.md:47`, `D/kin/data/SCHEMA-NOTES.md:14`) |
| `contains` and `likely` become one “Contains” line | Present in print, web and no-JS. This conflicts with drafts preserving possible-contact or uncertain warnings. (`src/build_print.py:18–19`, `src/build_print.py:38–41`, `src/template.html:469`, `src/template.html:491–494`, `src/sup_nojs.py:12–14`, `D/kei-coffee/data/SCHEMA-NOTES.md:5`) |
| Numeric dollar prices | Print and no-JS require numbers; web multiplication coerces `null` to zero. There is no unknown-price handling in these formatters. (`src/build_print.py:15–17`, `src/template.html:434`, `src/sup_nojs.py:9–11`) |
| Flat price/add-on model | Renderers handle keyed price variants and direct add-ons. They do not traverse the drafts’ nested `optionGroups`, location branches or course structures. (`src/build_print.py:51–75`, `src/template.html:507–522`, `src/sup_nojs.py:15–23`, `D/vox/data/SCHEMA-NOTES.md:55–57`, `D/qua/data/SCHEMA-NOTES.md:46`) |
| Thirteen languages and English baseline | Language lists are duplicated across common code, print, web and fallback labels. Persian/Arabic/Urdu directionality and Chinese script mapping are explicit. (`src/build_common.py:9`, `src/build_print.py:5`, `src/build_print.py:27–28`, `src/build_print.py:115`, `src/template.html:416–420`, `src/template.html:435`, `src/sup_nojs.py:3–5`) |
| Every translation value must be nonempty | This is incompatible with draft dictionaries that intentionally retain empty descriptions. Missing descriptions must be represented consistently without inventing copy. (`src/build_common.py:44–53`, `D/nep/data/strings.en.json:153`, `D/nep/data/strings.en.json:159–161`) |
| SUP content provenance | Structure embeds SUP Toast/chart source descriptions; image provenance maps specific SUP dishes and storefronts. These records cannot become another brand’s provenance. (`src/structure.json:38`, `src/structure.json:55`, `src/assets/items/manifest.json:2–17`) |

### 3.3 Palette, typography and fixed layouts

- **Web palette:** red `#E5342B`, deep red `#B4231C`, ink `#1B1917`, body `#4A4542`, muted `#625B56`, ground `#F6F2ED`, surface `#FFFFFF`, line `#D8D0C8`, soft line `#E9E3DC`, control `#837A74`, warning background `#FCEAE8`, amber `#9A5A0B`, amber background `#FFF3DE`, amber line `#F0D3A3`. Theme metadata also fixes a white/light presentation. (`src/template.html:6–7`, `src/template.html:27–30`)
- **Print/card palette:** repeats SUP red/ink/body/muted colors; print also repeats line/amber tokens. They are separate literals and must be coordinated explicitly. (`src/print_template.html:10–16`, `src/qrcard.html:9–19`)
- **Latin typography:** Barlow Condensed display and Noto Sans body, with system fallbacks. Card directly requests these Google fonts. (`src/template.html:31–32`, `src/print_template.html:7`, `src/print_template.html:15–16`, `src/qrcard.html:4–8`)
- **Script typography:** Noto Sans KR, SC, TC, Arabic, JP and Devanagari; Noto Sans for Russian; Noto Nastaliq Urdu for Urdu. Script-specific fallback stacks and line-height rules are embedded separately in web and print. (`src/template.html:35–45`, `src/template.html:299–307`, `src/print_template.html:18–28`, `src/print_template.html:101–116`, `src/sup_fonts.py:11–13`)
- **Layout:** print is Letter with half-inch margins and two columns; card is exactly five by seven inches; web sets its own width/thumbnail dimensions. These are product presentation defaults, not restaurant identity, but remain fixed assumptions when copying. (`src/print_template.html:9`, `src/print_template.html:57`, `src/qrcard.html:6–13`, `src/template.html:33`)

### 3.4 Assets, filenames, storage and offline protocol

| Assumption | Evidence |
|---|---|
| Brand image inputs | Web always reads `assets/icon.png`, `logo.png`, `doodle.jpg`, `bowl.jpg`, `kimchi.jpg`; print requires `assets/logo.png`. The bowl/kimchi reads still execute even if their substitution markers are absent from a template. (`src/build.py:40–49`, `src/build_print.py:14`) |
| Dish image convention | Thumbnail names are item IDs under `assets/items`; full images are under `assets/full`; variant pairs are `<item>-<key>.jpg` and `<item>-<key>-thumb.jpg`. (`src/build_print.py:20–24`, `src/build.py:17–38`) |
| SUP variant map | Explicitly maps bao, wings, lomo, cajun, fried rice and kimchi options. (`src/assets/variants/map.json:2–30`) |
| Public asset layout | Copies items to `img/`, full images to `img/full/`, variants to `img/var/`; logo is copied as both `img/logo.png` and `img/social-logo.png`. (`src/build_site.py:18–25`) |
| Generated menu names | `sup-menu.html`, `print-<lang>.html`, `pdf/SUP-Menu-<lang>.pdf`. PDF references repeat in packaging, web footer, no-JS and both validators. (`src/build.py:50`, `src/build_print.py:121`, `src/build_print.py:191–193`, `src/build_site.py:17–23`, `src/template.html:583`, `src/sup_nojs.py:41`, `src/verify_pdfs.py:15`, `src/release.py:62`) |
| QR/card names and geometry | `assets/qr-menu.png`, public `img/qr-menu.png`, `qrcard.html`; caller requests nominal 2048-pixel QR. Generator snaps output to whole module pixels and uses its own fixed logo proportion. (`src/build_site.py:33–42`, `src/qr.swift:14–16`, `src/qr.swift:28–34`) |
| Font filenames | `assets/sup-fonts/` → public `sup-fonts/`; `sup-<language>.css`, `sup-<hash>.woff2`, `sup-<family>-OFL.txt`, `sup-manifest.json`. Runtime loads a relative `sup-fonts/sup-<lang>.css`. (`src/sup_fonts.py:27–51`, `src/build_site.py:45`, `src/template.html:899`) |
| Two different manifest roles | Root `sup-manifest.json` is the worker file allowlist; `assets/sup-fonts/sup-manifest.json` is font provenance/glyph coverage. The root manifest is not an installable-app web manifest. (`src/sup_sw.py:5–14`, `src/assets/sup-fonts/sup-manifest.json:2–8`, `src/assets/sup-fonts/sup-manifest.json:86–103`) |
| Language preference | Reads/writes `sup-lang`. (`src/template.html:457`, `src/template.html:697`) |
| Allergen preference | Writes/clears/reads `sup-avoid`. (`src/template.html:730–733`, `src/template.html:1210`) |
| Cache names and deletion | `sup-menu-<revision stamp>`, `sup-cache-state`; cleanup deletes other cache names beginning **`sup-`**, not just `sup-menu-`. (`src/sup-worker.js:3–4`, `src/sup-worker.js:16–17`) |
| Active-cache marker | `/sup-active` inside `sup-cache-state`; both activation and request fencing depend on it. (`src/sup-worker.js:16`, `src/sup-worker.js:22–28`) |
| Worker generation names | `sup-worker.js`, `sup-manifest.json`, substitution token `__SUP_MANIFEST__`. (`src/sup_sw.py:7–14`, `src/sup-worker.js:2`) |
| Root behavior | Manifest prepends `/` to every file, aliases `/` to `/index.html`, precaches `/index.html` and `/img/logo.png`. Registration occurs only on `/` or `/index.html`, using `/sup-worker.js` with scope `/`. (`src/sup_sw.py:6–9`, `src/template.html:967–976`) |
| Root-specific cache policy | Full-photo detection uses `/img/full/` and `/img/var/`; PDF range handling uses `/pdf/`; warming uses `/sup-fonts/` and `/img/`. (`src/sup-worker.js:7`, `src/sup-worker.js:59–64`, `src/template.html:973`) |
| Photo-cache message | `supOpened` payload is constructed as an origin-root path. Worker accepts messages only from the origin’s SUP index document. (`src/template.html:978`, `src/sup-worker.js:69–75`) |
| Offline metadata | Response header `X-SUP-Offline`, meta name `sup-offline`, UI ID `supOffline`. (`src/sup-worker.js:43–45`, `src/template.html:962–964`) |
| Other SUP-prefixed identifiers | `window.supFontReady`, `supFonts`, `supQuery`, `sup-nojs`; these are page-local identifiers rather than cross-page storage namespaces, but remain naming assumptions. (`src/template.html:654`, `src/template.html:895`, `src/template.html:914`, `src/sup_nojs.py:24`) |
| Kill switch and revision salt | `SUP_SW_DISABLED` controls generation; `|sup-sw-disabled=` affects revision hashing. (`src/sup_sw.py:8`, `src/build_common.py:41`) |

### 3.5 Orchestration, release allowlist and importer

**The complete public-file allowlist is:**

- `index.html`, `qrcard.html`, `revision.json`, `.nojekyll`
- `img/logo.png`, `img/social-logo.png`, `img/qr-menu.png`
- Every direct `.jpg`/`.png` file from `assets/items`, `assets/full`, `assets/variants`, mapped to their public image directories
- All thirteen `pdf/SUP-Menu-<lang>.pdf` files
- Every direct file from `assets/sup-fonts`, under `sup-fonts/`
- `sup-worker.js`, `sup-manifest.json`

The actual recursive file set must equal that set exactly. Sibling folders, sources, PRDs, research and hosting configuration are not allowed output additions. (`src/release.py:58–67`)

Additional fixed assumptions:

- Source hashing includes the web, print, QR, card, worker, font and no-JS sources together, all thirteen dictionaries and all nonhidden asset files except generated `qr-menu.png`. `verify_pdfs.py` and `merge_toast.py` are not in that explicit script list. (`src/build_common.py:10–12`, `src/build_common.py:26–28`)
- Release requires five search/offline keys, the complete web bundle, exact worker generation and a `sup-nojs` fallback. The documented 221-key count is current data; code checks parity and the required subset rather than a literal count of 221. (`src/build_common.py:14–15`, `src/build_common.py:44–54`, `src/release.py:49–76`, `src/BUILD.md:34`)
- Release always preflights Poppler, runs all three builders and replaces `site`, `pdf`, `sup-menu.html` and thirteen print HTML files. It additionally copies the generated QR back into assets. (`src/release.py:135–170`)
- PDF gates require ASCII dollar-price sequences and Letter dimensions. Contact gates require SUP’s exact website/email. These need tier/brand-aware inputs. (`src/release.py:77–81`, `src/release.py:107–125`)
- Platform assumptions are macOS Chrome’s fixed application path, `sips` for web image dimensions, Swift/CoreImage/Vision for QR, and Poppler for release validation. Only the relevant subset is necessary for a smaller tier. (`src/build_print.py:4`, `src/build.py:19–21`, `src/qr.swift:1–3`, `src/qrread.swift:1–3`, `src/build_common.py:17–24`)
- Toast import fixes `research/toast-out.json`, the SUP dish/variant name map, an Irvine/Buena Park provenance string and a manual `sidebroth` assignment. Matching includes prefix matches; unmatched names print warnings rather than aborting. The script overwrites `structure.json`. (`src/merge_toast.py:2`, `src/merge_toast.py:11–17`, `src/merge_toast.py:18–30`, `src/merge_toast.py:39–49`)

## 5. Decisive separability verdict

### Yes — without executing the other product layers

The evidence is the actual call path:

1. `build_print.py` imports only shared string/revision helpers from project code, then reads structure, dictionaries and logo. (`src/build_print.py:2–14`)
2. Its `build(lang)` renders sections and substitutes the print template, producing `print-<lang>.html`. (`src/build_print.py:76–121`)
3. Its `to_pdf()` opens that local HTML in Chrome, waits for document fonts and invokes `Page.printToPDF`. (`src/build_print.py:123–172`)
4. Its main block defaults to all thirteen languages and calls those two functions for each PDF. It does not call `build.py`, `build_site.py`, worker generation or QR tools. (`src/build_print.py:189–195`)
5. The QR and worker calls instead live in `build_site.py`. (`src/build_site.py:27–46`)

### The source-file dependency remains

At import time, `build_print.py` calculates `revision(root)`. That hashes every named `SOURCES` file, including `build_site.py`, web template, worker source, QR Swift sources and card template, plus local assets. Removing those files while leaving hashing unchanged causes file reads to fail **before PDF rendering**. (`src/build_print.py:8`, `src/build_common.py:10–12`, `src/build_common.py:26–41`)

Therefore:

| Meaning of “standalone” | Answer |
|---|---|
| Produce PDFs from the intact source workspace without running web, worker or QR stages | **Yes.** (`src/build_print.py:189–195`) |
| Copy only the print renderer/template/content/logo and discard all other source files, unchanged | **No.** Shared revision hashing still requires them. (`src/build_common.py:10–12`, `src/build_common.py:30–41`) |
| Use current `release.py` as a print-only verified command | **No.** It always builds and verifies the full product. (`src/release.py:147–149`, `src/release.py:58–81`) |
| Create a genuinely reduced, verified print-only package with bounded changes | **Yes, as an implementation conclusion:** split input hashing and orchestration/gates while retaining the existing PDF exporter. (`src/build_common.py:10–12`, `src/release.py:107–125`, `src/build_print.py:123–195`) |

No fresh rendering success is claimed; the user prohibited builds.

## 6. Multi-tenancy risk to live SUP

### Current boundary: sound for distinct sibling paths

The worker normalizes only configured aliases and intercepts only enabled, same-origin GET requests whose exact path appears in `SUP.files`. It does not have a catch-all navigation fallback. Thus `/vox/…`, `/nep/…` and other distinct sibling paths bypass it when absent from SUP’s manifest. Adding seven siblings does not change this predicate. (`src/sup-worker.js:5–6`, `src/sup-worker.js:48–51`, `src/BUILD.md:26`)

**Control is not offline coverage.** A root-controlled sibling page still has its own requests bypassed. Conversely, a sibling page requesting `/img/logo.png` is requesting a SUP-owned URL, so SUP may serve that request. The guard checks the requested URL, not “which restaurant page initiated it.” (`src/sup-worker.js:48–55`, `src/sup_sw.py:9`)

### Failure modes

| Risk | Consequence and evidence |
|---|---|
| **Critical: copied SUP cache namespace** | A sibling worker retaining `sup-cache-state` writes the same `/sup-active` marker. Retaining `sup-` cleanup can delete SUP’s cache; the SUP worker then sees a different active marker and loses cache access. Merely changing the worker URL or scope is insufficient. (`src/sup-worker.js:3–4`, `src/sup-worker.js:16–28`) |
| **Critical: replacing root worker or root index with a sibling build** | Root registration uses `/sup-worker.js`, scope `/`; generated packages all name their page `index.html`. An incorrectly placed sibling package can replace SUP’s root page or worker. This is a deployment-placement risk, not an operation performed by this audit. (`src/template.html:976`, `src/build_site.py:17`, `src/sup_sw.py:13–14`) |
| **High: generating SUP’s manifest from an aggregate eight-brand tree** | Manifest generation recursively includes every file under the supplied tree. If that tree contains siblings, SUP acquires their URLs unless generation is redesigned. The current release allowlist rejects those extra files; relaxing it without separating worker ownership would defeat the documented boundary. (`src/sup_sw.py:5–9`, `src/release.py:58–73`, `src/BUILD.md:26`) |
| **High: treating SUP’s output directory as the aggregate site** | Direct `build_site.py` deletes its existing `site/`; verified release replaces that directory wholesale. Siblings stored inside that output tree are not preserved. This affects local output and becomes a live risk only if a publisher mirrors that result. (`src/build_site.py:10–17`, `src/release.py:153–162`) |
| **High: destructive host-root synchronization** | The saved routing decision specifically requires preserving `CNAME` and every brand directory when synchronizing SUP’s build into the repository root. The actual publishing command/configuration was not verified here. (`N:32`, `CNAME:1`, `src/BUILD.md:7`) |
| **High: root-relative assets or missing slash handling** | Sibling references accidentally resolving to `/img/…`, `/pdf/…` or `/sup-fonts/…` can display/cache SUP assets. Slug-prefixed social-image paths also fail the current package-root reference resolver unless adapted. (`src/template.html:15–20`, `src/template.html:482–487`, `src/template.html:583`, `src/template.html:899`, `src/release.py:98–106`) |
| **Medium: shared preference keys** | Copied pages use the same origin’s `sup-lang` and `sup-avoid`, so one brand can overwrite preferences later read by SUP. A pathname does not create a separate localStorage namespace. The code contains no brand dimension in those keys. (`src/template.html:450–457`, `src/template.html:697`, `src/template.html:730–733`, `src/template.html:1210`) |
| **Medium: sibling offline support silently absent** | The page’s registration guard accepts only `/` and `/index.html`. Copying it to a slug leaves the menu online-only despite shipping worker files. Root SUP control does not fill this gap because sibling requests bypass its file list. (`src/template.html:967`, `src/sup-worker.js:50`) |
| **Medium: partial worker path migration** | Updating only manifest paths is insufficient: `/pdf/` range handling, full-photo classification, warm requests and permitted message sender still assume root SUP paths. Offline PDFs or viewed photos can regress independently of ordinary online rendering. (`src/sup-worker.js:7`, `src/sup-worker.js:59–75`, `src/template.html:973–978`) |
| **Medium: kill switch applied to copied namespaces** | Disabled-worker activation still writes the state marker and performs `sup-` cleanup before unregistering. A copied sibling kill switch can therefore disable/delete SUP cache state even though the sibling worker intercepts no requests. (`src/sup-worker.js:16–18`, `src/BUILD.md:32`) |
| **Unquantified: aggregate offline storage** | The implementation caches visited assets/PDFs and has no per-brand storage budget or eviction policy beyond old-revision cleanup. Eight menus increase potential storage demand. Actual browser quota, eviction behavior and device impact were not measured. (`src/sup-worker.js:17`, `src/sup-worker.js:54–64`, `src/sup-worker.js:75`, `src/BUILD.md:28`) |

### Boundaries to preserve during any future implementation

These are implementation requirements inferred from the current code, not a publication recommendation:

- Keep SUP’s generated manifest limited to SUP-owned paths; maintain exact-path bypass for siblings. (`src/sup_sw.py:5–9`, `src/sup-worker.js:48–50`)
- Give each offline brand an independent registration scope, cache/state namespace and deletion prefix. A name such as `sup-vox-*` is still inside SUP’s current deletion range. (`src/template.html:976`, `src/sup-worker.js:17`)
- Keep sibling assets under their own base paths and make every relevant URL/validator agree on that base. (`N:28–33`, `src/release.py:98–106`)
- Separate per-brand build outputs from the composed hosting tree; preserve the root SUP files, `CNAME` and unrelated brand directories during host updates. (`src/build_site.py:10–17`, `src/release.py:153–162`, `N:32`)
- Validate fallback, PDFs and JavaScript against the same brand/location data contract; a shared JSON shape alone does not guarantee equivalent meaning. (`src/sup_nojs.py:12–42`, `D/rol/data/SCHEMA-NOTES.md:17`, `D/vox/data/SCHEMA-NOTES.md:5`)

## Final verdict

**The other brands do not need the full QR-code web product to obtain thirteen-language print menus.** PDF rendering is already a distinct execution path. The work needed for a smaller product is to separate revision inputs and validation, replace SUP identity, and support the actual draft data correctly. (`src/build_print.py:189–195`, `src/build_common.py:10–12`, `src/release.py:147–149`)

**The seven drafts are real, but they are English review prototypes with richer schemas—not completed thirteen-language SUP replacements.** Their existing content and adapted renderers are useful starting points; translating them or feeding them unchanged into SUP’s renderer would not resolve their documented gaps. (`D/vox/data/SCHEMA-NOTES.md:5`, `D/vox/data/SCHEMA-NOTES.md:69–71`, `D/nep/PRD.md:19`, `D/kin/REPORT.md:25–27`, `D/rol/REPORT.md:9–15`, `D/ini/REPORT.md:15`, `D/kei-coffee/data/SCHEMA-NOTES.md:3–5`, `D/qua/REPORT.md:13`)
